newsitem.title: SPAIN: Nuclear asset, debt transfer seen positive - Fecsa.
newsitem.headline: Nuclear asset, debt transfer seen positive - Fecsa.

text.p: A transfer of Fuerza Electricas de Catalunya's (Fecsa) nuclear assets off its balance sheet to form a new company would be good for the Catalan utility as long as the transfer included debt, Fecsa's chairman Juan Echevarria said on Tuesday.
"Naturally (the segregation) would imply an economic compensation. We have to transfer both assets and debt," he told reporters ahead of Wednesday's shareholders' meeting.
Parent Empresa Nacional de Electricidad is proposing the asset transfer.
Echevarria said Fecsa's current debt level was 172.5 billion pesetas, but declined to say how much of that corresponds to nuclear debt.
Regarding the possibility of Fecsa forming a new gas and coal company with Enher, as local reports have indicated, Echevarria said that this would make gas and coal assets more efficient.
The chairman was not ruling out a larger than two percent reduction in the electricity tariff next year, and highlighted the positive effect that removing coal subsidies would have on the tariff.

Wednesday's shareholders' meeting is due to approve a reduction in the maximum number of shareholders, as well as incorporate Joan Hortala, chairman of the Barcelona stock exchange, and Antonio Costas Comensana as new board members.

Shareholders will also approve last year's accounts. Fecsa posted group net profit of 13.51 billion pesetas in 1996 versus 15.39 billion pesetas the year earlier, and a total dividend of 55 pesetas gross per share.
